articles.title: 'Risky and Gutsy': Resident Evil Movie Star Austin Abrams Reveals His First Reaction to The Film's 'Shocking' Finale
articles.summary: Resident Evil movie star Austin Abrams has recalled his initial reaction to the film's finale, which he believes is "crazy and shocking."
articles.body:
Resident Evil movie star Austin Abrams has recalled his initial reaction to the film's finale, which he believes is "crazy and shocking."

Warning: spoilers for Resident Evil follow...

Zach Cregger's enjoyable Resident Evil film follows Abrams' everyman courier Bryan as he transports a bag of medical supplies into a deadly zombie apocalypse. Unfortunately, as you'll know from watching the film, Bryan ends up not making it out of Raccoon City alive.

It's a particularly sad ending for Bryan as he's never able to reconnect with his pregnant girlfriend, or make amends with her after an earlier argument. Despite fighting off waves of undead and recording a message of reconciliation for her, Bryan succumbs to his injuries and turns into a monster, just as a cure is produced.

Cregger's ending is certainly a bold choice, and one that differs from the heroic end featured in every Resident Evil game. But Abrams himself is clearly a fan of this story's finale, and described the ending as a "risky and gutsy" decision by Cregger, in an era where downbeat endings are now rarer to avoid bumming out audiences and killing a movie's chance for word-of-mouth recommendations.

"I've been living with it for a while now, but I thought it was crazy and shocking when I first read it," Abrams told The Hollywood Reporter . "I love that Zach takes those risks. You follow this one guy the whole time, so hopefully you’re enjoying watching him and rooting for him. Then to have him not make it is really risky and gutsy, which is what I love about all of Zach’s work. So I was surprised by it, but I also loved that he would take that chance.

"With a lot of movies nowadays, they’re a little too afraid to do something like that — to kill off a character you really like," he concluded. "And if they do, the blow is softened in some way so it doesn't hurt too much. Whereas a lot of older films don’t do that; they just rip your heart out. We're here to feel, man. We're here to go through something. So I'm just appreciative that Zach is willing to take a risk like that."

With all of that said, however, we learned this week that Cregger still tweaked the film's ending in post production using material he'd already shot — if anything to make things even more tragic. There's details here of how things would have originally planned out .

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Microsoft is laying off 268 Xbox staffers and Ninja Theory may close
articles.summary: Deals to sell off Ninja Theory fell through over the summer.
articles.body: Microsoft is laying off around 260 Xbox employees today, as part of an ongoing “reset” of its gaming business. 1,600 Xbox employees were impacted by layoffs in July, with Xbox CEO Asha Sharma describing the cuts as “the most significant restructure in Xbox history.” Today’s layoffs are part of the 3,200 roles that were previously confirmed to be impacted over the course of Microsoft’s 2027 financial year (which ends in June 2027). “We are eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the XGS management and central functions layer,” says Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty in a memo. “The actions completed since July, inclusive of the studio divestitures, bring us roughly three-quarters of the way through previously announced restructuring. I am deeply grateful for what our colleagues have built, and I know how difficult today will be for those leaving and the teams around them.” The Xbox restructuring also includes Microsoft selling off four Xbox studios as part of its significant gaming cuts. While two studios, Double Fine and Compulsion Games, have already gone independent, deals to sell off Ninja Theory have fallen through. As a result, Microsoft is now proceeding with a consultation period to close the studio, unless the company can find another buyer. “Unfortunately, two separate agreements for Ninja Theory fell through,” explains Booty. “We will now begin consultation with employees on a proposed closure while continuing to explore other paths forward.” The deal to sell off Undead Labs is still proceeding, and Booty says it has “now successfully transitioned on similar terms” to Compulsion and Double Fine. Xbox is also still in consultations over the future of Arkane and the Blade game, in accordance with French labor laws. “Consultation with Arkane remains underway and is expected to continue through the end of the year,” says Booty. Today’s Xbox layoffs are also part of a larger reorganization of Xbox today. Activision is taking on the Halo franchise, alongside Sea of Thieves and World’s Edge, the studio responsible for Age of Empires. You can read more about the latest Xbox shake-up right here.

articles.title: Xbox is barely Xbox anymore
articles.summary: More changes and layoffs at Xbox signal a further retreat from Microsoft’s gaming brand.
articles.body: Xbox has become a shell of its former self — and things are only getting worse. As part of its planned cuts impacting around 3,200 workers, the company announced today more changes that will further dilute the brand. Studios are being consolidated, others are on the brink of being closed altogether, and Xbox’s most iconic franchise, Halo, is being moved to a new developer. The future of Xbox looks more uncertain than ever. Today’s news includes “eliminating 268 roles across Halo Studios, other first-party studios, and the [Xbox Game Studios] management and central functions layer.” But there is also plenty of reorganization happening, particularly when it comes to Xbox subsidiary Activision Blizzard. Development of Halo is moving over to Activision, helmed by “a new, purpose-built team” that is separate from the Call of Duty teams. Halo Studios will continue to exist, for now, primarily as a support studio. Meanwhile, Sea of Thieves developer Rare and Age of Empires studio World’s Edge are both moving under the Activision umbrella. Similarly, Obsidian is being moved out from Xbox Game Studios and under Bethesda Game Studios, where it will refocus on the Fallout franchise, and all of Microsoft’s casual games, like Minesweeper and Solitaire, are moving under Candy Crush developer King. Meanwhile Playground and Turn 10, the studios responsible for Fable and Forza, are merging into one. This is all part of the Xbox “reset” outlined by new CEO Asha Sharma, which kicked off with 1,600 employees being laid off in July, with 1,600 more planned over the following fiscal year, leaving many employees in an awkward state of limbo. A pair of studios were also spun off from the company, with both Double Fine and Compulsion going independent. Today’s layoffs are part of that second wave that was previously announced. The reason for all of the changes, according to Sharma, is to eventually become a company that reaches “more than a billion people each day,” a nearly impossible goal that will be especially challenging to pull off given all of the cuts. The plan is to focus on known hits like Minecraft, Halo, and Candy Crush, while eschewing everything else and reevaluating just how much the company is investing in its Game Pass subscription service. “For Halo, our goal is clear: make the greatest Halo game ever, worthy of its universe and legacy, while staying true to what made players love it in the first place,” Activision president Rob Kostich said in a statement. “It is a bold ambition, one that this franchise deserves. We have already begun assembling a purpose-built team, unique in capability and talent, ready and excited to deliver this next chapter with the community.” [Image: Some of today’s moves, like expanding King and focusing more on franchises like Halo and Fallout, fit into that framework. But they also yet again raise a question that has plagued Microsoft’s gaming division for the last few years: What even is Xbox? Once upon a time it was clear: It was a console business that also developed and published exclusive games for the platform. But as Microsoft attempted to expand, particularly by spending billions of dollars to turn Game Pass into a Netflix for games, the brand was diluted. The console became increasingly unimportant, and as for exclusives, well, it’s hard to follow just what the plan is for those. Despite some superficial rebranding, the case for Xbox isn’t any clearer now. Today’s changes make that even more pronounced. Xbox Game Studios was once a sprawling organization of game developers creating titles for Game Pass and the various Xbox consoles. But after waves of layoffs, closures, and spinoffs, there isn’t all that much left under the umbrella. Today it consists of just a handful of studios like Gears of War developer The Coalition and Wasteland studio InXile. And the fate of these teams feels increasingly precarious. What happens to The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day launches next month? History suggests it won’t be anything good. After all, Halo Studios just released a well-received Combat Evolved remake in July, and now it has been reduced to a “small team” that “will continue supporting the Halo community and games in-market.” Xbox still plans for a future in the hardware business through whatever “Project Helix” ends up being. But when it comes to games, Xbox is mostly just Activision Blizzard and Bethesda now. Almost all of its most notable new games are coming from these subsidiaries, all of which were acquired for billions of dollars, initially to boost Game Pass. Recently, these companies have announced far-off titles like Fallout 5 and StarCraft in an apparent attempt to show that everything is okay while the broader Xbox business is embroiled in chaos. And now we have Activision making Halo games. It’s a further signal that Xbox is attempting to make its franchises as big as possible — Activision managed to do just that with the annual juggernaut that is Call of Duty — but also a sign that the traditional Xbox brand is less important than ever. And that’s something no amount of capital letters will change.

articles.title: Undead Labs has completed its separation from Xbox.
articles.summary:
State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs is now an independent employee-owned studio. It’s the third studio to successfully separate from Xbox, after Double Fine and Compulsion Games did the same recently. “Development of State of Decay 3 remains actively underway at Undead Labs,” says the team. The game is still planned to release in 2027 on Xbox (and Game Pass), PC, and PlayStation.
Sadly, it looks like Ninja Theory won’t be the fourth Xbox studio avoiding closure, though.

articles.title: LEGO Teases Dragon Ball Sets
articles.summary: LEGO has released a short teaser video announcing that at least one Dragon Ball LEGO set is coming soon.
articles.body:
Rumors have been percolating around the internet for a while, but LEGO just confirmed it: Dragon Ball LEGO sets are coming soon.

A short video teaser posted to LEGO’s website and social pages shows six Dragon Balls gathered, followed by a seventh rolling in. Then the screen flashes to a blue-and-red Dragon Ball logo, followed by a LEGO logo and “Adults Welcome.” That means we can expect at least one LEGO Dragon Ball set, and possibly more, aimed at adult LEGO builders , rather than kids.

Assuming this teaser plays out like other recent LEGO announcements, we can expect to see details of LEGO’s upcoming Dragon Ball set(s) in the coming weeks.

For now, there’s no word on any specific Dragon Ball sets or release dates. The furthest-out release date for any announced LEGO sets is January 1, which is when the LEGO Super Mario minifigure sets will hit store shelves (some of those sets are available for preorder now).

Dragon Ball was created by Akira Toriyama as an anime TV series that ran from 1986 - 1989 in Japan. It has since turned into a whole franchise of additional TV series, movies, video games, and more.

LEGO’s teaser shows six Dragon Balls, yellow-orange spheres with varying numbers of red stars on them. While six Dragon Balls together have no special power, introducing the seventh makes them able to summon their Eternal Dragon, who can grant wishes. That’s what’s implied when the seventh ball rolls in during the teaser video, right before it ends.

This new Dragon Ball joins a growing list of anime-themed sets, including One Piece , KPop Demon Hunters , and Pokémon . For more, check out the release dates for all upcoming LEGO sets announced so far.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Undead Labs Goes Independent After Xbox Separation, Confirms State of Decay 3 Is Still In Development
articles.summary: Undead Labs has confirmed that State of Decay 3 is still in development after the studio separated from Xbox, becoming an independent, employee-owned developer.
articles.body:
Undead Labs has confirmed that State of Decay 3 is still in development after the studio separated from Xbox, becoming an independent, employee-owned developer.

Undead Labs shared this information in a September 22 blog post , where they revealed that State of Decay 3 is currently in alpha, with plans to enter a closed beta by the end of 2026. The game is scheduled to launch in 2027 on Xbox, Game Pass, PC, and PlayStation.

“Independence brings us closer to our community and lets us focus on what matters most: making the best games we can and earning the continued support of the people who choose to spend their time with us. State of Decay exists because millions of players have made that choice over the years, and we’re dedicated to honoring their trust," Studio Head of Undead Labs Phillip Holt said in a statement.

“We’re enormously grateful for our years as part of XBOX and for everything that relationship has made possible. Microsoft has been part of the State of Decay story from the very beginning, and we’re proud of everything we’ve accomplished together.”

While the latest round of Xbox layoffs has resulted in some baffling business decisions that are leaving fans equal parts confused and concerned, players are largely welcoming Undead Labs' most recent announcement, particularly the fact that the studio is now owned by its own employees.

"Employee owned? That's awesome, happy for the crew! I think that is a great sign that the team really believes heavily in the work they've put into State of Decay 3," one user wrote on Reddit .

"Independent but keeping it on GamePass... has to be the biggest double win I've seen in a long time. Devs get their studio and subscribers still get to play it. While people who canceled their GamePass just outright buy it," another said.

"Nice to have some seemingly good news. Not a small feat to free themselves from Xbox," another wrote.

Xbox's latest shakeup comes as part of its continued restructuring that began this summer. Perhaps the biggest takeaway from today's events is the news that Call of Duty developer Activision is now taking over development of Halo , with Rare also shoved under their umbrella.

This follows Xbox's divestment of several other studios over the last few months. One of the most notable of these was Psychonauts developer Double Fine, which has managed to stay afloat in the aftermath and was even given full ownership of its IPs in the amicable separation. It seems that Undead Labs has also followed this path, and is still going full-speed ahead to give players its next game.

IGN's Michael Highham got the chance to play a 30-minute demo for State of Decay 3 at Gamescom this August, and walked away from his time with the game feeling like it showed "a lot of promise."

"Even as an early alpha build, I got a good impression of the improved gunplay and movement, and the general feeling that this is a State of the Decay worthy of the current generation while building on the series' fundamentals," he wrote.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .
